10 days in Canada.

all my life i had dreamed of visiting Canada, i have no idea why, but i've always felt drawn to the place. i found out when i was about 10, that my maternal grandfather knocked back a job offer to work with the RCMP because, and i quote "it was too cold" (a scotsman saying canada was too cold made no sense in my tween mind). turns out he would have been working in Saskatchwan, so i get it now. when i heard that story, i was more adamant than ever that i NEEDED to go to Canada.

fast forward 15 years, and i finally got the chance. my SO had to travel to Vancouver for work - it could not have been more perfect! he paid for my flight, arranged 5 extra days on the work dollar and we were off.

while he was locked in some conference room at UBC, i was free to do whatever i wanted. i toured the campus, went to some museum just behind it, strolled along the nudist beach (it was early may, and still cold, so no nudity anywhere - i did see a dead crab though). i even walked, yes WALKED, from UBC to downtown Vancouver. the most beautiful 3 hour walk i have ever had. strolled around town, found a pub and ordered a beer at the bar.

the next day, our canadian host drove us to Banff. we ate at Denny's for lunch, I had a Wendy's root beer, and we had a fuel stop at the top of a mountain and poked at the melting snow. i'd never seen avalanche tunnels before, nor even knew of their existence, and i was amazed. i nerded out when i realised we were driving through a valley that had been carved by a glacier, and i learned the international signal for "hey mister truck driver, can you please honk your horn for me?".

the 2 nights in Banff are a blur of beer, 3am rye, and elk burgers, a trip up Sulphur Mountain, Canadian coffee at the Fairmont, and being stalked by a coyote. plus a hungover drive to Drumheller to see the Tyrell Museum, and eat a picnic in an ancient river bed filled with mysterious fossils.

there was also teaching Canadian baristas what a "cafe latte" was, and enjoying their hilarious attempts at producing one. we ate at the revolving restaurant, and closed off the trip with sushi before heading to YVR for our trip home.

so many fond memories, and my itch for Canada was made worse after seeing it.
Western Canada is beautiful! I'm glad you could find inspiration here (my home country). Thank you for sharing.
thank you for having such a beautiful country, with such open and friendly people. i can't wait to find my way back again.

I was in Nepal a couple of years ago and had to travel by public bus from Kathmandu to Pokhara. You know what Nepal's most known for? Mountains. You know where all their roads are? The sides of mountains. These narrow, barely maintained strips of pavement or sometimes dirt traversed by not just buses, but trucks, cars, motorcycles, mopeds, bicycles, pedestrians, stray dogs and goats. Seriously, like a lot of goats.

See the thing about Nepalese drivers, is that their impatient. I get it, there's a lot of 'traffic' on the road and you've gotta get to where you're going, so you honk that horn! And you speed. Yes, you push down on that accelerator because the brake will only slow you down right? Oh, and that car that is slightly ahead of you? You bet your ass I'm gonna speed up and overtake you on the narrowest road upon the highest cliff face using that crumbly verge off into nothingness. Vertigo. Hello old friend.

Now back to the interior. If that wasn't enough, the other thing that public buses need in order to be profitable in Nepal is passengers. Lots and lots of passengers. Hey you and your sixteen mates! Sure, we can fit you. I may have a small Tibetan woman sitting on my lap and the man across the aisle has a chicken, but just crowd on in. Oxygen is for pussies. I'm already holding my breath anyways since that man with the meat bag got on an hour ago.

So yeah, that 5 hours was pretty memorable.

P.S: Loved every minute! It's an amazing country and people and I recommend everyone go!
